newsitem.title: CANADA: New legal threats against Bre-X questioned.
newsitem.headline: New legal threats against Bre-X questioned.

text.p: Threats of another lawsuit over the ownership of Bre-X Minerals Ltd's rich Busang gold deposit appear opportunistic, analysts say.
"I don't understand the merits of this," said gold analyst Chad Williams with Research Capital Corp in Montreal.
"People should consider this as blatant opportunism."

The previous owners of Busang I, a small part of the rich gold discovery, have asked to be involved in Bre-X's negotiations with PT Krueng Gasui, a Bre-X partner in Indonesia that has threatened to sue unless Bre-X discusses its claims of up to 40 percent of the entire gold deposit.
The previous owners say their claims "mirror" PT Krueng Gasui's claims, Bre-X said in a release early Friday.
Bre-X said it had received a letter from Canadian lawyers acting for Waverly Mining Finance Plc, Montague Gold NL, Westralian Resources Projects Ltd and William McLucas which threatened legal action.
Bre-X said in its statement that the claim is "without foundation" but could not be reached for further comment.
"They're just piggy-backing on (Jusuf) Merukh," said gold analyst Catherine Gignac with Deacon Capital.
Merukh controls Bre-X partner PT Krueng Gasui.

In July, Bre-X announced a deal with the previous owners to transfer the Busang I property into Bre-X's hands. Montague Gold NL released a letter saying the agreement with Bre-X "removes any doubts over the ownership of these relevant interests."
But the statements may not stand up in Canadian courts, said Gignac.
"It's an annoyance to Bre-X, and they have to address it."
Lawyers for Krueng Gasui told Bre-X to take steps to resolve that dispute before today or they would take the matter to court.
Bre-X has said it was willing to talk with the lawyers, but Merukh told Reuters in Indonesia on Friday that it had not heard from Bre-X yet.
The ownership disputes have interfered with Bre-X's progress at the Busang property. Indonesian government officials have delayed issuing necessary contracts of work to Bre-X because of the dispute.
But a source in Indonesia told Reuters today that the Mines Minister had forwarded mining contracts to the president for final approval. The source did not know if Bre-X's permits were among them.
Without the permits, Bre-X could have difficulty finding a major partner to take over part or all of the property, analysts have said.
But Bre-X said in its statement Friday that it "does not intend to be diverted from its corporate objectives by this kind of opportunism."

Exploration at the Busang properties on the island of Borneo has outlined at least 47 million ounces of gold. Some analysts predict the area may contain up to 100 million ounces, making it one of the world's largest gold deposits.
-- Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104
